_about.purpose: Seed dataset of common ECU connection guides. Pin numbers and functions are FACTS transcribed from publicly-readable sources (transpondery.com HTML tables, ECU forum threads, vendor public spec sheets). Facts about a chip's pins are not copyrightable — see https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/17/102 ; only the specific visual layout/diagram is protected, which is why this dataset ships pin tables ONLY (no copied images). The user can add their own connector photos in the editor.
_about.scope: 10 entries covering the most common Bosch / Continental ECU families for European tuning work. Bench/OBD wiring focuses on the essential pins: power, ground, CAN, K-Line. Pinouts are partial — verify against the official service literature or your tool's documentation before connecting to real hardware.
_about.disclaimer: WIRING INFORMATION FOR REFERENCE ONLY. Wrong wiring can permanently damage the ECU. Verify the pinout against your specific vehicle/variant before powering anything on. The bundled entries cover Socket K (one of typically several connectors on a real ECU) and are sufficient for OBD / bench reading but not for full vehicle wiring.

pins.notes: Ignition power; switch ON during read

entries.warnings: Ensure a stabilised 13.5 V supply — voltage drops below 12 V mid-write can brick the flash. Always read and back up the full file before any write. The MED17 firmware is checksum-protected; recalculate and write the checksum on every modified file or the ECU will reject the image on next boot.
entries.notes: Source: transpondery.com (https://www.transpondery.com/pinouts/vag/med17/med1711_pinout.html). Same Socket K layout shared by MED17.1, MED17.1.6, MED17.5 family — verify variant before use.

entries.warnings: Verify checksum after every write. EDC17 firmware is signature-protected on newer variants — older tools may need a boot-mode read first to extract the EEPROM and TC1797 keys.
entries.notes: Source: transpondery.com (https://www.transpondery.com/pinouts/vag/edc17/edc17c46_pinout.html). Common on 2.0 TDI CR engines (CFFB/CFGB/CFHC/CGLC etc.).

entries.warnings: Recalculate and write checksum after every modification. Boot-mode entry requires pulling the BOOT pin to GND on the TriCore TC1796 die — refer to your tool's documentation for the exact contact pad.
entries.notes: Source: transpondery.com (https://www.transpondery.com/pinouts/vag/edc17/edc17cp04_pinout.html). Found on 3.0 V6 TDI engines.

entries.warnings: MED9 generation supports K-Line diagnostic — older tools can read via OBD/K-Line without bench wiring. Always back up the file before write.
entries.notes: Source: transpondery.com (https://www.transpondery.com/pinouts/vag/med9x_pinout.html). MED9.1 family covers 1.8T, 2.0T, 2.5T petrol engines from approximately 2002–2010.

entries.warnings: Immobiliser PIN data lives at addresses 0x12E–0x12F in the 24C04 EEPROM. EDC15 is normally read via OBD/K-Line — bench wiring rarely needed. Older variants (pre-2003) may use only K-Line; later variants add CAN.
entries.notes: Source: transpondery.com (https://www.transpondery.com/pinouts/vag/edc15_pinout.html). EDC15P+ / EDC15VM+ / EDC15C2 share this layout. There is also an 80-pin variant — see EDC15 (80-pin) entry.

entries.warnings: Family-wide entry — covers EDC16U1 / EDC16CP / EDC16CP34 / EDC16U31. Specific variant pin numbers may shift slightly; verify against the variant before connecting.
entries.notes: Source: transpondery.com (https://www.transpondery.com/pinouts/vag/edc16_pinout.html). Common on TDI Pumpe-Düse engines circa 2004–2009.

entries.voltage: 13.5V regulated (15V Kl.15, 30V Kl.30 indicated in service literature)
entries.warnings: Mercedes EDC16CP31 covers CR4.11 / CR4.12 / CR4.20 / CR4.xx 'MB CR' part-number series. Risk of immo desync if EZS/CAS sync block is lost — back up the full file before any write.
entries.notes: Source: transpondery.com (https://www.transpondery.com/pinouts/mercedes/edc16cp31_pinout.html). Found on OM642 V6 CDI and OM651 4-cyl CDI engines.

entries.voltage: 12V (mix of 15V and 30V supplies in service docs)
entries.warnings: Mercedes CR2.x / CR1.x series — older common-rail diesel ECUs. Three separate socket bodies (S1/S2/S3); ensure correct identification before bench wiring.
entries.notes: Source: transpondery.com (https://www.transpondery.com/pinouts/mercedes/edc15_pinout.html). Compatible MB CR signs: CR2.39, CR2.14, CR2.35, CR2.36, CR1.2, CR1.7.

entries.warnings: BMW EDC16C35 used on E60/E83 X3 2.0d/3.0d engines. ISN-protected — back up the full file before write to preserve the ISN sync block.

SIMOS18 (TriCore TC1791) requires boot-mode entry for unsigned reads — see bri3d/Simos18_SBOOT toolchain on GitHub. Once unlocked, OBD CAN-based reads work with Autotuner / KESS3 v2 sessions. Coding tables and immo block (Tprot) are signature-protected — never write without a verified checksum recalc.
entries.notes: Source: community-aggregated facts from MHH AUTO + bri3d/Simos18_SBOOT (https://github.com/bri3d/Simos18_SBOOT). Common on Audi A3 8V / VW Golf 7 GTI EA888 Gen3 1.8/2.0 TFSI.
